q-100250.name: Question 1
q-100250.worked_solution:
Applying the quotient rule, we get

$$
{lim}_{x\to 2}\frac{3x}{\sqrt[3]{2{x}^{4}-5}}=\frac{{lim}_{x\to 2}3x}{{lim}_{x\to 2}\sqrt[3]{2{x}^{4}-5}}
$$

We calculate the limits of the numerator and denominator, separately.

For the numerator, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to 2}3x & =3{lim}_{x\to 2}x \\  & =3\cdot 2 \\  & =6\,.\end{aligned}
$$

Applying the root rule in the denominator, we have
 

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to 2}\sqrt[3]{2{x}^{4}-5} & =\sqrt[3]{{lim}_{x\to 2}(2{x}^{4}-5)} \\  & =\sqrt[3]{2(2)^{4}-5)} \\  & =\sqrt[3]{27} \\  & =3\,.\end{aligned}
$$

Consequently,

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to 1}\frac{3x}{\sqrt[3]{2{x}^{4}-5}} & =\frac{6}{3}=2\,.\end{aligned}
$$

q-338364.worked_solution:
From the graph, we get that ${lim}_{x\to \,2}f(x)=3.$

From the product rule, we have

$$
{lim}_{x\to \,2}(x-1)^{2}\,(f(x)-2)^{3}={lim}_{x\to \,2}(x-1)^{2}\cdot {lim}_{x\to \,2}(f(x)-2)^{3}.
$$

We calculate the limits of each factor, separately.

Applying the power rule, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to \,2}(x-1)^{2} & ={({lim}_{x\to \,2}(x-1))}^{2} \\  & =(2-1)^{2} \\  & ={1}^{2} \\  & =1\,,\end{aligned}
$$

and

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to \,2}(f(x)-2)^{3} & ={({lim}_{x\to \,2}(f(x)-2))}^{3} \\  & =(3-2)^{3} \\  & ={1}^{3} \\  & =1\,.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to \,2}(x-1)^{2}\,(f(x)-2)^{3} & =(1)\cdot (1) \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$
